content: We're doing an architecture review for Q3 and I want to propose replacing our custom service discovery with Consul. We built the current system two years ago and it's become a maintenance burden — we spend more time fixing discovery than building features.

Consul gives you service discovery, health checking, and KV storage in one package. The main consideration is the operational overhead of running the Consul cluster itself — 3 or 5 servers for the consensus group.

We're on Kubernetes so I'd run it as a StatefulSet with 3 replicas. The thing is, I also want to use Consul Connect for service mesh — right now we have a homegrown mTLS setup that's fragile and nobody understands except me. Having a bus factor of one on the mTLS infrastructure is a risk.

Consul Connect with transparent proxy would replace both your custom service discovery and the homegrown mTLS. Envoy sidecars handle the mTLS automatically, and service intentions give you an access control layer.

Right, and the service intentions are declarative — I can define 'service A can talk to service B' in code rather than managing certificate rotations manually. Fundamentally this is about replacing bespoke infrastructure with community-supported tooling. We're not in the business of building service meshes.

That's a strong argument for the review. The team's time should go toward business logic, not infrastructure that's already a solved problem. The migration path from your current setup to Consul would be the main thing to plan carefully.

Agreed. I'll propose a phased migration — run Consul alongside the existing discovery for a month, migrate services one at a time, then decommission the old system. Same blue-green pattern we use for app deployments, just at the infrastructure level.
